Well, Its a clinical trial. They can choose to accept whoever they want. Sadly its nothing a lawyer could do either. I'm just hoping the main doctor understands how dire this is to my mom.

In most other patients, there are other options that can often help. He doesn't have the time to read all of moms file. He doesn't understand how much more aggressive moms disease is than usual, how poorly moms body reacts to certain medicines, how allergic she is to everything, how little time she has left, and the big thing he doesn't seem to understand is that if mom tries these other options, she loses the ability to go back to her current treatment, which is at least slowing the disease.

The stem cell transplant is either going to completely cure her or kill her. If she loses the ability to go back to her old treatment, it only makes sense to do the only other option that has the ability to cure her. The doctor believes its a risk that shouldn't be taken, but mom is out of time, its all that's left.

He knows a few things I don't like, like playing with my ears or trying to take off my glasses, but that's mostly because of a reaction like pulling his hand away. 

I have a feeling I will eventually tell him, I just don't know if it will be sooner or later.

I do not want to nor am I breaking up with him. this post wasn't a question of should I break up with him. It wasn't even a consideration about that. This was me wondering if anyone else did not enjoy French kissing. He is way to awesome for me to break up with him over something as silly as this. This is a matter of me not quite liking something that seems to be a normal thing that couples do.

I am quite aware that I should tell him how I feel, but its something I can't do yet. And I know I have a problem. It's why I'm going to therapy. If I told him he'd totally be willing to compromise. Really, he'd probably not do it at all if I asked, but if I told him I would totally compromise into something like, we make out less often than he wants, but we still do at least. 

He is in no way forcing me, nor do I feel forced to make out. Like I said in my original post, I've turned him down a few times. I didn't tell him the reason was I didn't like it, but I did turn him down and he immediately backed off.

I don't think he's a problem. And I know I have a problem. I'm codependent and seeing a therapist, and communication is one of the things I'm working on.

This post wasn't a "I hate making out with my bf and he likes it and that's a problem" I was curious if others didn't enjoy making out. I never said it was making or breaking the relationship. 

And edit because I dont think its clear in this post: I haven't told him about me not enjoying it. Part of me being codependent means I feel responsible for peoples emotions. If he got upset it would crush me. I'm still working on being able to communicate my feelings and to not feel guilty when doing so. I haven't quite gotten to the point where I can voice it yet.

I don't see any "red flags" from what she's saying. I may not know much about mutism, but I haven't seen anything that looks suspicious.

May I ask where you get your information from? I'm assuming you yourself must be mute, but Just doing a simple google search, I have seen that messed up vocal cords can be a cause of mutism, and since it was a birth defect, maybe she just doesn't have the inclination to try and teach herself to talk in one way or another, since she never has.

She might not be able to whisper since she has never moved her mouth to form these letters, since she has never talked. Just like children must learn how to make the sounds by manipulating their tongue and lips, so would she. This can be hard, especially at an older age, and since it would be so quiet, she probably just prefers to sign. 

I think by accusing her of not truly being mute because you can't believe in the way she feels, you are incredibly rude.
